body.en: Your community has identified that a nearby stream overflows almost every rainy season, but nothing has changed about how close houses are built to it. As a resident, what's the most effective risk-reduction step you can push for now, before the next rainy season?

choices.label: Advocate with the assembly for a buffer zone and proper drainage along the stream, and support it publicly
choices.consequence: Right focus. Disaster risk reduction works best before the disaster, not after — fixing the underlying exposure (building too close, poor drainage) prevents the same flood from repeating every single year.

choices.label: Just make sure your own house has sandbags ready each time it rains
choices.consequence: This only protects you, and only partially. It does nothing about the underlying risk your whole community keeps facing year after year.

choices.label: Assume it's not fixable and just accept it as normal
choices.consequence: This is exactly the assumption that lets recurring, preventable disasters keep repeating. Most flood risk from stream overflow is addressable with drainage and buffer planning.
